newsitem.title: ITALY: Italians catch 82 illegal immigrants, find skeleton.
newsitem.headline: Italians catch 82 illegal immigrants, find skeleton.

text.p: Authorities on the remote Italian island of Lampedusa said on Thursday that they had apprehended 82 illegal immigrants crammed into a small boat from Tunisia in their first such interception of the year.
The skeleton of a man was also caught in fishermen's nets, a grim reminder of the risks run by immigrants who pay to travel in small boats for the crossing from North Africa.
"Doctors who examined it said it had been in the sea for about three months," police lieutenant Pietro Spana, head of aerial and naval operations on Lampedusa, said by telephone.
He said the skeleton, still draped in ragged jeans, was found on the night of January 18 -- the same night as the illegal immigrants.
Lampedusa, midway between Sicily and the North African coast, is a magnet for thousands of illegal immigrants.

They are ferried from the island to Sicily and served with expulsion orders. Authorities acknowledge that many of the foreigners ignore the orders and stay in Italy or move on to other European countries.
Spana said the 82 included six people from Zaire and four women. The two crew of the small vessel were arrested, he said.
Police film of the interception, made available to Reuters, showed the foreigners packed like sardines on the deck of the vessel, the Khaled, as they were escorted into port.
